{{Short description|Swiss mathematician (1930–2011)}}
[[File:Heinrich-Kleisli-1987.jpeg|thumb|right|Heinrich Kleisli in 1987]]
'''Heinrich Kleisli''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|k|l|aɪ|s|l|i}}; October 19, 1930 – April 5, 2011) was a [[Swiss (people)|Swiss]] [[mathematician]].  He is the namesake of several constructions in [[category theory]], including the [[Kleisli category]] and [[Kleisli triple]]s.  He is also the namesake of the [[Kleisli Query System]], a tool for integration of heterogeneous databases developed at the [[University of Pennsylvania]].

Kleisli earned his Ph.D. at [[ETH Zurich]] in 1960, having been supervised by [[Beno Eckmann]] and [[Ernst Specker]].  His dissertation was on [[homotopy]] and [[abelian categories]].  He served as an associate professor at the [[University of Ottawa]] before relocating to the [[University of Fribourg]] in 1966.  He became a full professor at Fribourg in 1967.

== Selected publications ==

* Kleisli, H., [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2034693 ''Every standard construction is induced by a pair of adjoint functors''] ([[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society|Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. '''16''']], [[American Mathematical Society|AMS]] 544-546) (1965)
